Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G5117; out of place, i.e. (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked:--amiss, harm, unreasonable.
BiblicalUsage: Out of place is the word for what is wrong, harmful, or wicked. The thief on the cross said this man has done nothing amiss, Festus was told to come down and accuse Paul if there was any wickedness in him, the islanders first thought Paul was a murderer and then changed their minds, and Paul asks prayer for deliverance from unreasonable and wicked men.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the thief's confession is the key to the word: Christ had done nothing out of place, and every charge against Him fell apart. The world still calls good men wicked, and I hold that the cross is where the charge was answered once for all.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
